decisions.reason: Report names the running dsh web host node.exe PID 42432 from running-processes.txt as the koffi.node loader, explains Windows locks the mapped .node binary until that process exits, and ties npm's copyfile EBUSY (attempt1-ebusy.log) to the blocked copy.

Explicitly states refresh only reloads the SPA while the host keeps running, and gives an ordered numbered procedure: stop/verify all dsh host and worker processes, run install from an external terminal, then restart and verify. It targets dsh-related processes only, not every Node process.

Grounded in npm-dist-tags.txt: bare name resolves to latest=0.1.1-rc.2 (alpha only on the alpha tag), so attempt 2 replaced alpha.4 with rc.2 — a downgrade, not a preserve/upgrade; correctly identified as the resolution mechanism, not a version-label slip.

Provides `npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.2-alpha.5 @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui` after stopping the host, then restart dsh web and verify `dsh --version` prints 0.1.2-alpha.5; explicitly warns @alpha is a moving tag and cannot substitute for the exact pin.

Advises README authors to never publish unpinned install commands, always pin exact tested core (and plugin) versions since a bare name follows latest and can silently downgrade prerelease users; accepts both pinned-combined and separate-command guidance, and no quoted BAD example is treated as endorsement.
